videos.summary:
HOW TO TOPROLL A TALLER TOPROLLER | DON'T FOLLOW YOUR INSTINCTS!

When you're facing a taller toproller, your natural instincts in the setup might be the very thing costing you the match.

In this video, I break down a subtle but incredibly powerful technique that changes how you approach the centre of the table against an opponent with a longer arm.

The secret? A strong, controlled SUPINATED RISE.

Instead of reacting to your opponent's hand position, fighting for height, or trying to match their setup, you need to completely IGNORE what they're doing and focus on establishing your own position.

By correctly combining supination with rising pressure, you can arrive at centre on your terms while making your taller opponent appear to be the one creating problems in the eyes of the referee.

The result? You establish your fundamental power, put your opponent under pressure, and make the referee your ally before READY GO is even called.

This is one of those small technical details that can completely transform your effectiveness against taller toprollers.

Stop reacting. Start controlling.

👇 Have you struggled against taller toprollers? Let me know in the comments.

videos.title: The CURSE of OVER TOPROLLING & How To ACTUALLY DEFEAT a STRONG CUP
videos.summary:
THE CURSE OF OVER TOPROLLING — How to ACTUALLY DEFEAT a STRONG CUP

The harder you try to TOPROLL someone with a powerful CUP, the more likely you are to disconnect yourself from your own strength.

It's one of the most common technical mistakes in armwrestling, and it's costing athletes matches they should be winning.

After 14 years of armwrestling, I've learned that sometimes the best way to defeat an opponent's strength is to stop trying to escape it.

When facing an opponent with exceptional cupping strength, our instinct is often to climb higher, attack their fingers and commit everything to pronation and back pressure.

But there's a fundamental problem.

The more aggressively you chase the toproll, the more vulnerable you can become to losing your own structural connection.

Your opponent cups.

Your arm opens.

Your pronation becomes disconnected from your side pressure.

And suddenly, despite being incredibly strong, you have no meaningful access to the power you need to win.

SO WHAT'S THE SOLUTION?

Instead of gripping higher and desperately trying to escape their cup, consider doing the opposite.

GRIP LOWER. GET INSIDE THEIR POTENTIAL CUP.

By deliberately positioning your grip slightly lower, you can allow your opponent to engage their cupping strength WITHOUT sacrificing your connection to pronated side pressure.

You're no longer fighting desperately to prevent their wrist from flexing.

You're positioning yourself so that even when it DOES flex, your fundamental power remains accessible.

This is where armwrestling becomes a game of intelligence rather than simply strength.

In this video, I explain:

🔹 Why overcommitting to the toproll can destroy your own power.

🔹 How a strong cup disconnects opponents who rely too heavily on back pressure.

🔹 Why gripping LOWER can actually give you a greater mechanical advantage.

🔹 How to maintain access to PRONATED SIDE PRESSURE even when your opponent successfully cups.

🔹 How to stop fighting your opponent's strongest weapon and start exploiting its limitations.

THE BIG LESSON?

You don't always need to STOP your opponent from doing what they're strong at.

Sometimes you simply need to make sure that what they're strong at DOESN'T MATTER.

Stop chasing the perfect toproll. Start protecting your access to power.

Because ultimately, armwrestling isn't about forcing your favourite technique onto every opponent.

It's about finding the position where YOUR strength remains connected and THEIRS becomes ineffective.
